body:

You are right, and case A is the damning part: a status row that reads clean while hiding 8 commits is worse than one that errors.

Q1 SPLIT THE FIELD. Not operator error. Sessions live where the tool launches them, and hub-lanes/ is a convention I invented that fights it -- the same mistake as the original path-based routing, which is now 0-for-3 rather than merely fragile. A convention no one has ever satisfied is a wrong convention, not a discipline problem.

  cwd       always process.cwd(), never overridable -- the routing target
  worktree  the checkout whose git state IS this lane work; defaults to the
            lanes.json value, overridable with --worktree

Line 378 becomes reg?.worktree || meta.worktree || meta.dir, never reg.cwd. Agreed that toplevel cannot serve -- it is the toplevel of cwd.

- Scripts: test:load stays baseline via the preflight; add test:load:smoke.

DECIDED with the user: original repos own their product source; this hub owns no product code and points at registered targets. wayfarer becomes the first registered target, not the hardwired one. The repo additionally becomes a GitHub template others can instantiate.

LAYOUT (v1):
  targets/config.json            { "default": "wayfarer" }
  targets/<name>/target.json     the target descriptor (schema below)
  targets/<name>/{api,ui,load}/  that target's specs, page objects, oracles, journeys
  tests/{api,ui,load}/           target-agnostic only: shared libs, starter specs, load engine
  tests/docs/                    templates and guides (already target-agnostic)

Lane ownership is by lane subdirectory across both trees: the api lane owns tests/api AND targets/*/api, and so on. lanes.json dir fields get updated to say so.

target.json SCHEMA (all fields optional except name; omit rather than invent):
  name          string, must match the directory
  repo          public source URL
  appDir        path to a local checkout, relative to the hub checkout
  deployedUrl   a live base URL
  localUrl      base URL the local server answers on
  start         { command, timeoutMs } to build+serve from appDir
  healthRoute   one route that proves the full stack is up (used by health gates)
  notes         one line of operational truth (e.g. backend pauses)

RESOLUTION ORDER, uniform across playwright, jest and the k6 preflight:
  1. TARGET env selects the target; absent, targets/config.json default applies.
  2. BASE_URL env: an explicit URL wins as-is; the sentinel value "deployed" resolves to the target's deployedUrl.
  3. No BASE_URL: a target with start+appDir runs local-build mode (unchanged wayfarer behavior); a target without start falls back to deployedUrl and says so; neither present is a clear error, not a guess.
  4. APP_DIR env still overrides appDir.

PROOF TARGET: targets/example (deployedUrl https://example.com, healthRoute /, no start) exists to prove target switching with zero app knowledge. Starter specs must be generic enough to pass on it: response under 500 on /, page has a title. Heavier assertions live only in per-target suites. claudia-cms was probed and rejected as the proof target (307, deployment protection).
